message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can check the current air quality in Los Angeles on a few reliable sources:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the AQI (Air Quality Index) and pollutant details. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles,” and see the live AQI, forecast, and pollutant breakdown. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Many local outlets publish daily air‑quality updates, especially during wildfire season. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., Plume Labs, BreezoMeter) | These apps provide real‑time AQI, health recommendations, and alerts. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles right now?” They usually pull data from AirNow or similar services.

Let me know if you’d like a quick summary of what the AQI categories mean or how to interpret the numbers!
